steps.say: Brackets hold extra information. The sentence must make sense without them.
steps.show: Lake Toba (in North Sumatra) is huge.

steps.say: A pair of commas can do the same job as brackets.
steps.show: Pak Joko, the school gardener, grows orchids.

steps.say: Hyphens join words that work together to describe a noun.
steps.show: a well-known singer     a ten-year-old girl

steps.say: A hyphen can change the meaning of a word.
Read your sentence aloud to check that the punctuation makes the meaning clear.

options.why: The hyphen should join sugar and free.
A comma does not join the words.
Brackets do not join describing words.

hints: Two words describe the drink together.
A hyphen joins words that work together before a noun.
Which two words describe the drink?
check.explanation: Sugar and free work together to describe the drink, so they are joined: a sugar-free drink.

check.prompt: Write the words that should go in brackets. Mount Rinjani which is on Lombok is a volcano.
hints: Read the sentence without some of the words. Does it still make sense?
Look at the words straight after Mount Rinjani.
check.explanation: Which is on Lombok is extra information, so it can go in brackets: Mount Rinjani (which is on Lombok) is a volcano.
